counterexample_measurability.f: Real-domain indicator of E, zero outside E
counterexample_measurability.Vn: V1 is identity on [1,2]; Vn=0 for n>=2
verified_steps: All input random variables are measurable.
Vn converges pointwise and hence almost surely to V.
f is identically zero on a neighborhood of 0, so ContinuousAt f 0 holds in the ambient topology.
The inverse image of {1} under f(V1) is E, so f(V1) is not measurable.
Finite exceptional initial indices do not prevent numerical convergence but violate an every-output measurability obligation.
counterexample_measurability.conclusion: Original explicit conditions cannot guarantee every composite output measurable, even under ambient continuity at S.
not_claimed: No new Lean counterexample was built.
This example does not make f(V) nonmeasurable: f(V)=0.
This does not by itself refute a correctly formulated numerical convergence theorem.

counterexample_relative_continuity.f: f(0)=0 and f(x)=1 for x!=0, a Borel measurable function
counterexample_relative_continuity.conclusion: Relative ContinuousOn f S holds, but f(Vn)=1 does not converge to f(V)=0. Adding Borel measurability alone does not fix an interpretation using only relative continuity.
